name: Make factory start resilient: remote checkout, git sync races and scoped startup checks
description:
## Summary

Between 16:40 and 17:18 MST on 2026-11-03, `$rowbly-factory` was started eight times on the `rowbly`
Board (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, low effort, main checkout on `main`). None of the runs started a worker.
Two were interrupted by the user within seconds and six stopped during startup checks. Seven
distinct failure modes caused this, and most of them recurred because nothing records what a
previous run learned. On every run the startup was all or nothing, so a fault on one machine or in
one Stage blocked the whole Board, even though thinkpad had free capacity (4 slots) and 14–15
Stories were eligible.

## Runs reviewed

| Settled (MST) | Thread | Outcome | Failure modes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16:40 | 64f91254 Run Rowbly Software Factory | Interrupted by the user 0.25 s after start, before any command; restarted 14 s later | none (restart) |
| 16:46 | c048bea7 Run the Rowbly Story Factory | Local `git sync` exit 4 `Rowbly capture changed; prepare again` | F3, F2, F5 |
| 16:55 | 8ebb7d85 Run Rowbly Software Factory | Interrupted by the user 1 s after start (probably to edit ROWBLY.md's Model Selection first) | none (restart) |
| 16:57 | 95db5f2f Supervise Rowbly Software Factory | Local `git sync` exit 4 `Git index changed before publication` | F4, F5, F8 |
| 17:04 | 526c183a Supervise Rowbly Board Factory | Rook `git sync`: `Automatic Merge Conflict Resolution is Off` | F1, F2, F7 |
| 17:12 | 5c34b106 Run the Rowbly Software Factory | In Refinement Stage Prompt moved Stories to "In Development", which does not exist; `pnpm` not found on rook | F6, F2, F7 |
| 17:15 | 990949c9 Supervise the Rowbly Story Factory | Rook `git sync`: Automatic Merge Conflict Resolution Off | F1, F2, F7 |
| 17:18 | 8052fc31 Run the Rowbly Story Factory | Same as above; rook's tree was clean, so the sync had nothing to publish | F1, F2, F7 |

## Failure modes and fixes

### F1. Rook's Git Plugin preference blocked startup (3 runs)

**What happened.** ROWBLY.md tells the supervisor to update rook's checkout "the same way":
`rowbly git sync`, then cleanup, then `git pull --ff-only`. Rook's Local State
(`~/Projects/rowbly/.rowbly/local.json`) had `synchronization.enabled: false`, so `rowbly git sync`
there failed with:

```
INTERNAL: Plugin "git" failed in its command: Automatic Merge Conflict Resolution is Off
hint: turn it off with `rowbly plugins disable git`
```

The thinkpad preferences had it On. Git Plugin preferences are personal (per checkout), so the
setting on one machine says nothing about the other. Rook's tree was clean (`git status --porcelain`
was empty), so the sync had nothing to publish and the start was blocked for no reason. Someone
turned the setting on at 17:19, after the last run.

The skill already says to check `synchronization.enabled` and to turn it on only when ROWBLY.md or
the user says so, otherwise ask. Two problems:

- ROWBLY.md's "(Automatic Merge Conflict Resolution On)" reads as a description, not as permission.
- The agents applied the skill's rule for the supervisor's own checkout and did not apply it to rook.
  One run saw the setting was Off and ran sync anyway; another never checked.

**Fixes.**
- **Skill:** "Update the checkout" applies to *every* checkout the factory updates, local or remote.
  Read `rowbly git show` there before syncing. Run `rowbly git sync` only when Rowbly has saved
  changes that are not yet committed (`git status --porcelain -- <Data Root>` is not empty).
  Otherwise go straight to `git pull --ff-only`. A clean checkout never needs Automatic Merge
  Conflict Resolution.
- **ROWBLY.md:** say explicitly that the supervisor may run
  `rowbly git configure --automatic-merge-resolution on --automatic-commits on --frequency change` on
  thinkpad and rook and tell the user.
- **CLI:** this is a precondition, not an internal fault. Throw an Expected `USAGE` (exit 2) error
  with the hint `rowbly git configure --automatic-merge-resolution on`, rather than `INTERNAL` (exit 1).
  The skill reference reads exit 1 as a bug to report and not retry.
- **CLI:** `src/services/plugins/invoke.ts` attaches `turn it off with rowbly plugins disable <id>` to
  every error a Plugin command throws. That hint is wrong for a Plugin's own validation errors. Only
  attach it for a crash in a hook, or let the Plugin supply the hint.

### F2. Rowbly could not be run on rook over SSH (5 runs)

**What happened.** ROWBLY.md says non-login SSH shells lack `node` and `pnpm`, and it gives a full
path only for `t3`. Every run that reached rook guessed the PATH and spent 2–4 calls doing it:

- `bash -lc …`, which failed with `pnpm: command not found`
- `~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.22.1/bin`, which holds only a `node` symlink
- `v24.16.0`, which does not exist
- `~/.local/share/pnpm/bin`, which was empty or wrong

Each run found (or failed to find) `~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.18.0/bin` again from scratch. One run
gave up and stopped the factory. Another ran `t3 thread list` outside the project and got
`No T3 Code project matches '.'`.

**Fixes.**
- **ROWBLY.md:** record one exact, tested way to run Rowbly on rook, next to the `T3=` line. For
  example `ROWBLY_REMOTE='cd ~/Projects/rowbly && ~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.18.0/bin/pnpm --silent dev'`,
  or a stable wrapper script on rook such as `~/bin/rowbly-dev`, so a node upgrade does not
  silently break it.
- **Skill script:** add a `prepare-checkout` subcommand to `launch-worker.mjs` (or a sibling
  script). It takes `--ssh --project --rowbly '<command>' --min-free-gb` and does the whole remote
  checkout update in one call:
  - free memory
  - `git status`
  - `git show`
  - sync if needed (F1)
  - cleanup branch and PR
  - `pull --ff-only`

  It returns one JSON result with a `reason` per failure. The supervisor then stops reconstructing
  the SSH steps by hand, the same way the launcher already removed that work for launches.
- **Skill:** have the script check the remote prerequisites first (`node`, `pnpm`/rowbly, `t3`,
  `gh auth`) and report each missing one, rather than letting the model find them by trial.

### F3. A person editing the Board during startup sync (1 run)

**What happened.** The local `git sync` took about 50 s. Meanwhile the user was moving
ROW-74…ROW-88 into In Progress in the TUI (for example ROW-75 `updatedAt 23:41:34Z`). The sync's
snapshot check (`gitSyncJournal.ts:297`) failed on all three of the CLI's internal attempts. It
exited 4 with `Rowbly capture changed; prepare again` and the hint
`Resolve the reported cause, then retry`, which names no cause.

The TUI's per-change Automatic Commits for those moves were deferred and stayed uncommitted until
a later capture commit. ROWBLY.md calls the supervisor the Board's "only writer", but nothing
checks for, or tells the user about, an open TUI.

**Fixes.**
- **CLI:** when the capture keeps changing, wait for the Data Root to go quiet (no change for a few
  seconds, bounded) before preparing again, rather than three immediate attempts.
- **CLI:** the error lists the changed paths (Story keys) and says another writer (such as the
  TUI) was saving at the same time. Mark it retryable in `details`.
- **Skill:** a startup sync that fails as retryable is retried after a short wait, up to a bound,
  with a one-line note to the user ("the Board is being edited; retrying"). Read `runs` only after
  sync settles, so the first start decisions use a stable Board.
- **Skill / ROWBLY.md:** at start, say that people may keep editing in the TUI. The supervisor is
  the only *automated* writer, and its syncs cope with a person's edits; it does not stop because
  of them.

### F4. Read-only git commands broke the sync's index check (1 run)

**What happened.** The supervisor ran `git diff` / `git diff --cached` in parallel with its own
`rowbly git sync`. The sync compares the raw bytes of `.git/index` before and after a 16 s window
that includes a fetch (`gitSyncJournal.ts:292` and `:325`). `git diff` and `git status` rewrite the
index's stat cache even when no content changed. The sync failed with exit 4
`Git index changed before publication`, and the agent reported a conflict that did not exist.
Editors, the T3 UI and shell prompts that poll `git status` cause the same thing.

**Fixes.**
- **CLI:** compare the index's *content*, not its bytes: `git ls-files --stage` (or the staged
  tree, `git write-tree`), so a stat-cache refresh is not a change.
- **CLI:** include this case in the existing prepare-again retry (`gitSync.ts:302`, `:407`).
- **CLI:** report a real staged change as a distinct, named error (which paths were staged), not a
  generic `CONFLICT`.
- **Skill:** never run git commands or Board commands in parallel with `rowbly git sync`; wait for
  it to finish.
- **Required test** (storage contract, per AGENTS.md): a stat-only index refresh during
  publication still ends in the complete new state.

### F5. The skill contradicts itself on a failed sync (all sync failures)

**What happened.** "Update the checkout" step 1 says "If it fails, stop and tell the user its
message". "Board persistence" says "If it fails, retry it once". Every agent took the first rule
and stopped on transient errors (F3, F4) whose hint said to retry. The exit-code table makes it
worse by mapping `CONFLICT` (exit 4) to "do not force without the user".

**Fixes.**
- **Skill:** one rule for every `git sync`, classified by error:
  - retryable or transient (capture or index changed, network): wait and retry, bounded
  - configuration (Off, no upstream): fix it when ROWBLY.md authorizes, otherwise ask
  - a real Rowbly or git conflict, or merge evidence: stop and report the commits involved
- **CLI:** give sync failures distinct, stable `details.reason` values, so the skill can classify
  them without matching on message text.

### F6. A Stage Prompt named a Stage that does not exist (1 run)

**What happened.** The In Refinement Stage Prompt said "move the story to "In Development"". The
Board's Stages are Backlog, TODO, In Refinement, In Progress, In PR and Done. The supervisor
treated this as a startup failure and stopped the whole factory, including In Progress and In PR.
The prompt was fixed afterwards (it now says "In Progress"). ROWBLY.md's Stages section still does
not describe In Refinement.

**Fixes.**
- **Skill:** check 5 ("What the Stage Prompts need") also checks every Stage a prompt names against
  `stages list`. On a mismatch, skip *that Stage* and report it. Do not stop the Board (see F7).
- **CLI (optional):** `software-factory stages` reports a warning when a Stage Prompt mentions a quoted
  Stage name that does not exist. `apply` already refuses a move to an unknown Stage, so a
  warning is enough.
- **ROWBLY.md:** add In Refinement to Stages (what it does, where it sends a Story).

### F7. Startup checks are all or nothing (5 runs)

**What happened.** "Before you start" says: if any check fails, start nothing. So:

- rook's sync preference (F1) and rook's PATH (F2) stopped thinkpad workers too, with 4 free local
  slots and 15 eligible Stories;
- one bad Stage Prompt (F6) stopped every Stage.

**Fixes.**
- **Skill:** scope each check to what it guards.
  - A failing machine is left out of capacity, and the factory runs on the machines that pass. It
    reports the machine and how to fix it, and checks the machine again later (each loop, or when
    the user says it is fixed).
  - A failing Stage is skipped and its Stories reported.
  - Only Board-wide failures stop the factory: Data Root, Plugin, a local sync conflict, or no
    machine and no Stage usable.
- **ROWBLY.md:** a remote machine's checkout update is per machine. It runs before that machine's
  first worker, not as a gate on the whole factory.

### F8. Hand edits to factory policy at start (1 run, and the reason for an interrupt)

**What happened.** The user edited ROWBLY.md's Model Selection just before a start (and interrupted
one run to do it). The skill's cleanup step would move a hand edit to a cleanup PR that is never
merged. The supervisor would then run on uncommitted policy from the working tree, which nobody
else (rook, workers) sees. Separately, a `git sync` committed two deleted Stage Prompt files
(`backlog.md`, `todo.md`) without comment. That was correct if Rowbly made the deletions, but the
skill's order (sync first, then porcelain) hides the difference.

**Fixes.**
- **Skill:** treat uncommitted changes to ROWBLY.md and Stage Prompt files as *policy*. Show the
  diff and ask the user to commit them (or commit them as ROWBLY.md's repository rules say, here
  directly on `main`) before starting. Never run on unpublished policy, and never send it to a
  cleanup PR.
- **Skill:** run `git status --porcelain` before `git sync` and report what the sync will publish.

### Not failures: the two interrupts

The 16:40 and 16:55 runs were stopped by the user within 1 s, before any command, and restarted
seconds later. Startup wrote nothing, so the restarts were safe. Nothing needs fixing beyond F8.

## Proposed order

1. **ROWBLY.md** (no code): the rook Rowbly command (F2), the sync authorization (F1), In Refinement
   in Stages (F6), and per-machine startup (F7).
2. **Skill:**
   - one sync-failure rule (F5)
   - sync only when needed, on every checkout (F1)
   - no parallel git (F4)
   - scoped startup checks (F7)
   - checks on Stage names in Stage Prompts (F6)
   - policy edits (F8)
   - the `prepare-checkout` script (F2)
3. **CLI:**
   - an Expected error and correct hint for sync Off (F1), and the Plugin hint in `invoke.ts`
   - index content comparison and retry, with its storage test (F4)
   - waiting for the Data Root to go quiet, and naming changed paths (F3)
   - `details.reason` on sync errors (F5)
4. Update `skills/rowbly/` references, `skills/rowbly-reference.md` and its copies, and
   `docs/user-guide.md` for any exit-code or hint change.

## Acceptance criteria

- A factory start on a Board with a clean rook checkout succeeds with rook's Automatic Merge
  Conflict Resolution Off; no `git sync` runs there.
- With rook unreachable or misconfigured, the factory starts workers on thinkpad and reports rook's
  problem with its fix.
- `rowbly git sync` succeeds while `git status` runs in a loop in the same checkout.
- `rowbly git sync` while a person moves Stories in the TUI either succeeds after the Data Root goes
  quiet, or fails with a retryable error that names the changed Stories. The supervisor retries it.
- A Stage Prompt that names an unknown Stage disables only that Stage, with a report.
- The supervisor reaches rook's Rowbly in one call using the command ROWBLY.md records.
